newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden's April 15 budget - summary of media reports.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's April 15 budget - summary of media reports.

text.p: Following is a list of items the Swedish media has reported as leaks from the minority Social Democratic government's April 15 supplementary budget proposal being announced at 1100 gmt.
New or expanded items are marked '*'.
*- Twenty billion crowns in total extra spending in 1997 and 1998 to boost employment and education.
*- This includes a 16.3 billion crown five-point programme of labour market measures in 1998, growing to 21 billion crowns in 1999 and 23.3 billlion in 2000.
*- Local authorities to get 4.0 billion crowns of the total to boost spending on health care and schools. The sum will be raised to eight billion crowns annually from 1998 to 2000.
*- Increased spending to be financed by a projected budget surplus of 13.9 billion crowns in 1998, up from a previous forecast of from a 10 billion crown surplus.
*- Extra spending on social reforms in 1999 will reach 15 billion crowns and 26 billion crowns in 2000.
*- Gross Domestic Product (GDP) expected to rise 2.3 percent in 1997 and 2.5 percent in 1998, after rising 1.1 percent 1996.
*- Consumer prices seen rising 1.8 percent in 1997, 1.5 percent 1998, 2.0 percent 1999 and 2.0 percent 2000.
*- Budget deficit seen at 2.1 percent of GDP in 1997, but in 1998 the government expects to meet its target of balanced books despite increased spending.

*- Unemployment forecast at 4.5 percent in 2000, down from an expected 7.9 percent in 1997. It is seen at 7.1 percent in 1998, 5.6 percent in 1999. The government had promised to halve unemployment to 4.0 percent by the year 2000.
*- Small companies to get 1.6 billion crowns next year.

*- Environmental subsidies for the agricultural sector will be increased, enabling full use of European Union subsidies. 700 million crowns to be allocated to an expansion of an environmental programme, half financed by EU.
*- If starting a new company, a person has a right to take leave of absence from work for six months.
*- Labour market policies will get 900 million crowns this year.
*- Education will get an extra 500 million crowns in 1997 and the annual sum will increase gradually to reach six billion crowns in 2000.
*- 15,000 new university places in 1998 to boost number of students and another 15,000 every year to the year 2000. Thereby, places for 60,000 new students will have been created from 1997 to 2000.
*- A trial trainee system in 1997.
*- Trials with skilled labour training will be expanded by 1,500 places this year and 4,300 next year.

*- Adult education to get another 10,000 new places this autumn and the number of students will increase gradually to reach 140,000 places by 2000. The students will get benefits corresponding to unemployment benefits.

*- 1.5 billion crowns will be allocated to boost growth in 1998 and the sum will reach 5.9 billion crowns in 2000. The programme includes costs for a planned railway, Botniabanan, on the east coast of Sweden and city infra-structure projects in the cities of Gothenburg and Stockholm.
- Lower electricity taxes for power intensive industries.
- Downscaling of plans for large cutbacks on dental care expenses.
- No cut back on personal assistants for the disabled.
- The government to allocate 1.1 billion crowns annually to expand Stockholm's traffic system.
- Early retirement for people close to the current retirement age of 65 and for longterm unemployed who are over 60 years of age.
- Unemployed to be allowed to work in health care, elderly care and child care with 90 percent of a regular salary, paid mostly by the government.

- Small companies to be given support. Currently small companies pay five percent less in fees on staff with total wages of less than 600,000 crowns and the government will propose to raise this to between 800,000 and 900,000 crowns.
